ratings_why.fun: Earns 8 over 7 because Scorch is both a cost and a resource: the same burn feeds Slag Row Journeyman, gets cashed by Spring-Bath Newt and Wet Cellar Keeper, or is used by Ember-Belly Newt to kill your own units into Regrow for Ottilie and Mother Atra, so every turn has a real heal-or-keep call.
ratings_why.distinct: Damage that carries between turns, self-harm as fuel and Heat that rides on any tribe's carry play unlike today's tribes, though Reforge itself is a familiar +1/+1 buff.

verdict_why: Two small wording fixes (Bellows-Boy's choice, Two-Tongs stacking) would make it better; the core needs no change.

points.text: Bellows-Boy says "up to 2" at End of Turn but not who picks the amount; say whether the player sets it or it always spends what it can.
Say whether two Two-Tongs Grinders stack (four times) or not, and how a golden one combines with a normal one.
Ember-Belly Newt killing a Scorched 1-Health unit with Regrow under Ottilie gives +2/+2 permanently each fight and triggers Mother Atra; name it as a build, it is the tribe's best combo line.
Spotted-Belly Barker is the one payoff that only reads Heat; letting it also read Scorch or Regrows would tie it into the burn web.
Nutrisco's empty-slot count pulls against Ottilie's wide Regrow board; that tension is good, keep both rather than merging the builds.

standouts.why: Ember-Belly Newt ties together Journeyman, Regrow, Mother Atra and Ottilie by damaging your own board on purpose.
Crested Konrad turns selling into moving Heat, a pivot card, and its Birds overlap is pure Johnny.
Spring-Bath Newt makes the burns you took worth stats, so Scorch becomes a bank you choose when to cash.

weakest.why: Coal-Fetcher Eft is a plain one-shot buff with no decision in it.
Spotted-Belly Barker does the one obvious job of turning Heat into Attack.
Brother Paracel is a flat everyone-buff; its interest comes only from Wet Cellar Keeper's ordering.

flags.note: Fumarole Spitter's pings scale with uncapped Heat from Tier 3; at 30 Heat it strips shields and finishes small units freely.
The Furnace's growth is quadratic in Heat, worse with Two-Tongs; worth a late-board sim.
Nutrisco at 30 Heat and 3 empty slots gives +90/+90 in fight; the designer already flags it for a sim.
Konrad with Birds on Fly South copies Heat without losing it, a slow loop across turns.
Bellows-Boy's "up to 2" doesn't say who picks the amount.
